Source: A 23-year-old woman is admitted to the inpatient psychiatry unit after her boyfriend reported she was “acting funny and refusing to talk.” The patient’s boyfriend states that he came home from work and found the patient sitting up in bed staring at the wall.
She was recently switched from phenelzine to fluoxetine.
Her temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 122/79 mmHg, pulse is 68/min, and respirations are 12/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air.
The patient remains mute and ignores any external stimuli.
She resists any attempt to change her position.
The patient is lying on the bed with her left arm raised and pointing at the ceiling.
The patient’s medical history is significant for depression.
When he tried to move her, she would remain in whatever position she was placed.
When he said her name or waved his hand in front of her, she did not respond.
